title: A fibre-avoiding closure neighbourhood at a nongeneric smooth-fibre point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], where $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and every local ring of $S$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$, with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume the corresponding point in $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field] is not the generic point of an irreducible component [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components]. There exist affine open neighbourhoods $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $s$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $x$, with $V\subseteq f^{-1}(T)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], such that $A$ is a Noetherian integrally closed domain and $V\to T$ is smooth of finite presentation (on rings $B$ has a presentation by finitely many generators and relations over $A$). Put $Z=\overline{\{x\}}\cap V$. For every $t\in T$, the inverse image $Z_t\subseteq V_t$ contains no irreducible component of $V_t$. If $\eta$ is the generic point of $T$, every $z\in Z_\eta$ satisfies $\dim\mathcal O_{V_\eta,z}\ge2$. Empty $Z_\eta$ is allowed.

source.place: EGA IV4 Proposition 21.14.3, proof reducing (i), first assertion, to (ii), first paragraph; fibre-component avoidance invokes IV3 9.5.3. Affine normal-domain shrinking is included in this preparation statement. Read in the online English EGA translation; local EGA IV4 WANTED.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ containing $s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Its ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Consequently its underlying space is Noetherian: a descending chain of closed sets $V(I_j)$ gives an ascending chain of radical ideals; their union is an ideal generated by finitely many elements and hence equals one member of the chain. Apply [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components] to $T_0$, whose stalks are the given normal domains. Its component $C$ containing $s$ is open and integral. Choose an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $s\in T\subseteq C$, again by the affine basis. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $A$ is a nonzero domain, and it is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth].

source.place: Tags 0357 (lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles), 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian); preliminary normal-domain base shrinking in EGA IV4 21.14.3.

proof.text: The ring $A$ is integrally closed. Indeed, apply [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product] to $S$ and its quasi-compact affine open $T$; quasi-compactness is [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. It gives $A\cong\prod_{i<n}A_i$ with all $A_i$ normal domains. Here $n\ne0$ because $A\ne0$. If $n\ge2$, the tuple which is $1$ in one factor and $0$ elsewhere is a nontrivial idempotent $e$, contradicting the domain identity $e(1-e)=0$. Thus $n=1$, so $A$ is isomorphic to a normal domain. Both nonzeroness and all local normality hypotheses used here were supplied in Step 1 or in the item.

source.place: Tag 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections), using the existing finite-product statement and the domain conclusion of Step 1.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ containing $x$ inside $f^{-1}(T)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Its map $g:W\to T$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] it is locally of finite presentation, and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives a finite presentation of $B_0$ over $A$. In particular $g$ is of finite type (the finitely many polynomial generators suffice, and affine morphisms are quasi-compact), and $B_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Put $D=\overline{\{x\}}\cap W$, a closed subset of $W$, and put $Q=\overline{\{s\}}\subseteq T$ with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure from [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. If $s$ corresponds to $\mathfrak p\subset A$, then $Q=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)$ and $s$ is its generic point. Continuity gives $g(D)\subseteq Q$.

source.place: Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), affine restriction; Schemes Tag 01J3, reduced induced closed subscheme. EGA IV4 21.14.3, first reduction paragraph.

proof.text: The complement of $D_s$ is dense in $W_s$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $W_s$ has the subspace topology of $g^{-1}(s)$, so $D_s$ is the closure of $x$ inside $W_s$. A generic point $\xi$ of a component of $W_s$ cannot belong to that closure: then $x$ generalizes $\xi$, which forces $x=\xi$ by maximality of the irreducible component $\overline{\{\xi\}}$, contrary to the hypothesis. This hypothesis persists from $X_s$ to its open subscheme $W_s$: a point generic for a component of an open is generic for its closure component in the whole space (take the closure and use maximality in both directions). Every point of $W_s$ lies in a component and is a specialization of its generic point. Thus every nonempty open of $W_s$ contains one of these generic points, all outside $D_s$, proving density. These assertions concern ordinary scheme points, as in [def-sc-generic-point] and [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Proposition 9.5.3, the density condition used in EGA IV4 21.14.3; elementary closure and generic-point argument on the initial fibre.

proof.text: Form $W_Q=W\times_TQ$ and the inverse image $D_Q$ of the closed subset $D$. The map $W_Q\to Q$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The residue field of $Q$ at its generic point $s$ is $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)=\kappa_T(s)$: localize $A$ at $\mathfrak p$ and then quotient by its maximal ideal, as in [def-weil-residue-field]. Hence the fibre and open complement at $s$ are precisely $W_s$ and $W_s\setminus D_s$. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-open-fibre-density] to $W_Q\to Q$ and $W_Q\setminus D_Q$. Step 4 verifies its generic density hypothesis. Obtain an open $H\subseteq Q$ containing $s$ for which $W_t\setminus D_t$ is dense in $W_t$ for every $t\in H$. The residue fields for these points are also unchanged by the closed immersion $Q\to T$, by the same localization/quotient calculation.

source.place: Tag 054X (lemma-nowhere-dense-generic-fibre), applied over the reduced closure of s; EGA IV3 9.5.3 supplies the same density-spreading input.

proof.text: Since $Q$ is closed in $T$, its subset $Q\setminus H$ is closed in $T$. Set $W'=W\setminus g^{-1}(Q\setminus H)$, an open neighbourhood of $x$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $x\in V\subseteq W'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and put $Z=D\cap V=\overline{\{x\}}\cap V$. The map $V\to T$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. It is locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], so [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives precisely the required presentation $B\cong A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$. Thus it is smooth of finite presentation between the requested affine neighbourhoods. The base $T$ has not changed since Steps 1--2; in particular its ring $A$ is still a Noetherian integrally closed domain.

source.place: Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize); final affine restriction of the preparation in EGA IV4 21.14.3.

proof.text: For the neighbourhoods fixed in Step 6, verify fibre-component avoidance. If $t\notin Q$, then $Z_t$ is empty since $g(D)\subseteq Q$. If $t\in Q\setminus H$, then $V_t$ is empty by the choice of $W'$. If $t\in H$, the dense open $W_t\setminus D_t$ restricts to a dense open in the open subspace $V_t$: every nonempty open of $V_t$ is open in $W_t$ and meets that complement. Its complement $Z_t$ therefore contains no irreducible component of $V_t$, since the dense open meets each component at its generic point. To justify the last assertion, the components are finite: $V_t$ is affine of finite type over a field and hence Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. The complement of all components other than a chosen component is a nonempty open meeting that component, so density forces its generic point to be outside the closed $Z_t$.

source.place: Proposition 9.5.3, application to the closure of s; explicit neighbourhood construction in EGA IV4 21.14.3, first reduction paragraph.

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $T$. If $Z_\eta=\varnothing$, the remaining assertion is vacuous. Otherwise take $z\in Z_\eta$. Every point of $Z$ is a specialization of $x$, so continuity shows that $\eta=f(z)$ is a specialization of $s$. In $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the prime of $\eta$ is $(0)$, since $A$ is a domain. Thus the inclusion of primes $\mathfrak p_s\subseteq(0)$ forces $s=\eta$. Write $\mathfrak q_x,\mathfrak q_z\subset B$ for the primes of $x,z$; then $\mathfrak q_x\subseteq\mathfrak q_z$ by the definition of the Zariski closure. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $B_{\mathfrak q_x}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B_{\mathfrak q_z}\cong\mathcal O_{V,z}$. Every chain of primes below $\mathfrak q_x$ is also below $\mathfrak q_z$, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] and the assumed bound give $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}\ge\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\ge2$.

source.place: EGA IV4 Proposition 21.14.3, first reduction paragraph, specialization inequality; prime-chain expansion using Stacks Tags 00E3 and 00KF.

proof.text: Finally $\mathcal O_{T,\eta}=A_{(0)}=\operatorname{Frac}A$ is a field: every nonzero element of the domain $A$ is inverted. Its maximal ideal is therefore zero. Apply [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] to $V\to T$, the point $z$ over $\eta$, and the corresponding point of $V_\eta$. It identifies $\mathcal O_{V_\eta,z}$ with $\mathcal O_{V,z}/\mathfrak m_\eta\mathcal O_{V,z}=\mathcal O_{V,z}$. Step 8 therefore gives $\dim\mathcal O_{V_\eta,z}\ge2$. This holds for every $z\in Z_\eta$ and completes all clauses.

source.place: EGA IV4 Proposition 21.14.3, first reduction paragraph, generic-fibre stalk equality; Stacks Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre) fibre-stalk quotient.

The delivery is one commit containing the item and its report, with no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are identical to the unsplit base copy (compared against clones/live, clones/side-live and the Q05 snapshot). There is no repair note for this item and no SGA source. All nine steps are correct against the statements of the cited nodes. S1: a Noetherian affine has a Noetherian space; 0357 (trf node) gives an open integral component, and an affine inside it has a Noetherian domain A. S2: the normal-sections product with A a domain forces n=1, so A is normal. S3: W is smooth by restriction, finitely presented by 01TQ, and Noetherian; Q is the reduced closure of s, Spec(A/p), and g(D) lies in Q. S4: the complement of D_s is dense in W_s, because a generic point in closure(x) would equal x by maximality and the T0 property. S5: the 054X node applies to W_Q over Q with generic point s; I checked it against more-morphisms l.6524, where 'nonempty open' is the same as 'open containing eta'; the residue fields over Q and over T agree. S6: removing g^{-1}(Q minus H) still leaves x, then an affine V is chosen. S7: the three cases are t outside Q, t in Q minus H, and t in H; V_t is Noetherian with finitely many components, and the generic point of each component avoids the closed Z_t. Advisory: finite type of V_t over kappa(t) is used without spelling out the base change, which is elementary from the Step 6 presentation. S8: z in Z_eta forces s=eta, and q_x contained in q_z gives dim O_{V,z} >= 2 via affine stalk localization and the chains-below-prime node. S9: O_{T,eta} is a field, so 0HA1 gives O_{V_eta,z} = O_{V,z}. I tested A^2_k at a closed point, a vertical point on a relative curve over a DVR (empty Z_eta, which is allowed), and a horizontal height-2 point; each of the two hypotheses is needed. Batch-5 flag on lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components: accepted. It is the generic Stacks 0357 lemma, neither the trace-formula nor the Poincare assumption gives it, its 60-node closure reaches no other trf, Poincare or assumption node, and many sfb nodes already cite it. All five tool_uses (0357, normal sections, reduced induced, 054X, 0HA1) are generic tools and none replaces a unit step.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_smooth_closure_fibre_avoidance_neighbourhood {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hnormal : ∀ s : S, IsDomain (S.presheaf.stalk s) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (x : X) (hdim : 2 ≤ ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (hnongeneric : ∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents (f.fiber (f x)), ¬ IsGenericPoint (f.asFiber x) C) : ∃ (T : S.Opens) (V : X.Opens) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ T), IsAffineOpen T ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧ f x ∈ T ∧ x ∈ V ∧ IsNoetherianRing Γ(S, T) ∧ IsDomain Γ(S, T) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed Γ(S, T) ∧ Smooth (f.resLE T V e) ∧ (f.appLE T V e).hom.FinitePresentation ∧ (∀ (t : T.toScheme) (C : Set ((f.resLE T V e).fiber t)), C ∈ irreducibleComponents ((f.resLE T V e).fiber t) → ¬ C ⊆ ((f.resLE T V e).fiberι t ≫ V.ι) ⁻¹' closure ({x} : Set X)) ∧ (∀ (η : T.toScheme), IsGenericPoint η Set.univ → ∀ z : (f.resLE T V e).fiber η, ((f.resLE T V e).fiberι η ≫ V.ι) z ∈ closure ({x} : Set X) → 2 ≤ ringKrullDim (((f.resLE T V e).fiber η).presheaf.stalk z))
